chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Yazeed, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

The one who is not able to maintain good relations with us, let him maintain good relations with the poor of our Shias; and the one who is not able to visit our graves, let him visit the graves of the righteous of our brethren.

key_terms.يَصِلَنَا: maintain good relations / keep ties with us

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they cannot visit the Imams' graves or maintain direct ties with them?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in al-Kafi, establishes a hierarchical model of connectivity where direct access to the Imam is substituted by engaging with the broader Shia community, specifically the poor and the righteous. It underscores the Shia concept of 'silat al-rahim' extending beyond blood relatives to include spiritual kinship, ensuring that social cohesion and spiritual merit are maintained even in the absence of the Imam's physical presence.
